newsitem.title: USA: Albright says Clinton to seek MFN renewal for China.
newsitem.headline: Albright says Clinton to seek MFN renewal for China.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Wednesday said she expected President Bill Clinton to seek renewal of Most Favoured Nation trading status for China, saying it would promote human rights there.
Speaking to reporters after a speech at the Gerald R. Ford museum in Grand Rapids, Albright said the United States had a "strategic relationship with China that needs to be nurtured."

"As far as Most Favoured Nation (MFN) for China, we are obviously going to be pressing in order to make sure that that is renewed. We believe that it is important for us to have a trading relationship with China," Albright said.
Albright said the debate on the MFN issue in the United States had basically set human rights against trade, but that "I think that the two are not contradictory."
"If we can have a good trade relationship with China, it creates an atmosphere where it is more likely that human rights and political freedom will be respected in China," she said.

Clinton has until June to decide whether to renew Beijing's MFN status, which gives China the same access to U.S. markets as most other trading nations. Congress then must decide whether to accept MFN renewal or vote to revoke it.

Many trade analysts have said they expect a tough fight on the matter in Congress because of concerns about human rights abuses, nuclear techonology sales and allegations that Beijing tried to influence U.S. elections through illegal campaign contributions.
House of Representatives Democratic Leader Richard Gephardt said earlier on Wednesday he will likely oppose China's MFN this year as he did last year.

Albright said one of the reasons that she was going to visit Hong Kong on July 1 for the handover of the British colony to Chinese rule is to emphasise U.S. support for preserving Hong Kong's current way of life and freedoms.
She said she wanted to "make very clear, emphasise and underscore, that we expect that the way of life of Hong Kong will be preserved."
